The test image shows corn stalks with extensive dark brown to shiny black discoloration on the external stalk rind, with necrotic brown leaf sheaths. This is characteristic of **anthracnose stalk rot** — the hallmark is the shiny black rind discoloration forming large blotches/streaks.

Key distinguishing features:
- **Shiny black discoloration** on the stalk rind (external, not internal like charcoal rot)
- Dark lesions that have **coalesced into large black blotches** along the stalk
- Not localized to nodes (rules out Physoderma stalk rot)
- No soft/slimy rot or collapse (rules out bacterial stalk rot)
- No small pycnidia dots pattern (rules out Diplodia stalk rot)
